Keep the seven existing directory globs. Verified disjoint from every other ticket's scope, so parallel_safe stays truthful and the retired fixtures/** overlap hazard does not return.
reason: T-080's scope is seven DIRECTORY globs: fixtures/{manifest,approval,seed,catalog,personas,golden,tests}/**. The frozen suite pins the manifest as a FILE at the fixtures root: test_e8_proofs.py:69 MANIFEST_REL = 'fixtures/manifest.json', re-read at test_e6_trust.py:294, and test_e8_proofs.py:526 does 'from fixtures.generator import apply, generate'. I ran the glob-ownership derivation across all 47 tickets: fixtures/manifest.json, fixtures/generator.py and fixtures/__init__.py match ONLY T-000's universal '**' glob, and T-000 is closed. fixtures/manifest/** matches paths INSIDE the empty scaffold directory, not the file. Worse than merely missing: test_e8_proofs.py:305-313 asserts no stray manifest.json exists anywhere under fixtures/ except the canonical path, so T-080 writing fixtures/manifest/manifest.json (its only in-scope option) trips that assertion and fails loudly. Blast radius: all 8 e8_proofs tests (target 8, currently 0) plus the 6 e6_trust tests that route through _manifest() (6 of target 26). subject: T-080 scope cannot create fixtures/manifest.json, fixtures/generator, fixtures/__init__.py

head: c5c2aa72f67afb34ac9cde46334e100a2a46679b
proposed: Preferred: amend the frozen test so _compose_services() resolves the include: fragments (or so the deployable assertion reads the fragments directly), matching the architecture the scaffold actually shipped. Alternative if you would rather not amend: rule that the four deployables are declared in the root docker-compose.yml after all, and retire the 'no ticket ever edits this file' clause in its header - but that collides with the existing include: entries and I do not recommend it. Third option: accept acceptance_pass_rate topping out below 100 and record it as a known, explained red for the run.
reason: The test (test_spec_criteria.py:741-751) asserts a compose service whose name contains buyer/merchant/exchange/trust exists. It reads services via _compose_services() (:280), a deliberately TEXTUAL parser of the top-level 'services:' block of the single file _compose_path() (:267) returns - the root docker-compose.yml. It never follows 'include:'. Verified against the tree: the root file's services: block declares exactly postgres, neo4j and redis; the four deployables live in apps/{buyer,exchange,trust,merchant}/compose.yaml, pulled in by the include: at docker-compose.yml:11-20, and all four fragments exist on disk. The root file's own header states the contract the test contradicts: 'the nine include: fragments below are pre-created empty stubs inside their owners' scope globs, so a service ticket fills its own fragment and no ticket ever edits this file.' So every service ticket can fill its fragment exactly as designed, 'docker compose config' can resolve all four, and this test stays red for the entire run. Because acceptance_pass_rate is target 100 with tolerance 0, this single test pins the run's top-line metric below target permanently and holds spec_criteria_passing at 7/8. Note docker-compose.yml is NOT among the 16 hashed files, so duplicating the four services into the root would cost no frozen byte - but it contradicts the file's stated design and would collide with the include: fragments on duplicate service names.
subject: test_spec_criteria.py::test_compose_declares_healthchecked_postgres_neo4j_redis_and_separate_deployables is unsatisfiable

head: 12b31dfe856dd0bff352e9132dbb3fbafb048c0f
proposed: Two viable options, and I recommend the second. (A) Amend the frozen suite to re-marker this test from T-065 to T-062 - defensible on the merits, since the docstring's assertion is about routing a typed claim INTO the dimension, which is scoring's job, and T-062 already owns the other ten catalog_claim_accuracy tests; because T-062 depends on T-065 both modules exist at T-062's build time, so it resolves with no new edge. Costs amendment 3 and a re-measure. (B) No amendment: record that T-065's sixth frozen test is graded only after T-062 lands, put that in T-065's packet so its worker does not thrash on an ImportError it cannot fix from inside its own scope, and close T-065 on its other five plus its own verify command. The metric is identical under both, so A buys ledger tidiness and B buys one fewer amendment.
reason: The test is marked ticket T-065 but imports 'from apps.trust.src.scoring import claim_dimension, score' (test_e6_trust.py:1470). apps/trust/src/scoring/** is T-062's exclusive scope. T-062.depends_on = [T-060, T-065, T-080] - it depends on T-065 - while T-065.depends_on = [T-010, T-021, T-060, T-080] has no T-062 edge. So T-065 schedules and is graded BEFORE T-062, and at that moment the module it imports does not exist; the import sits inside the test function, so it is an ImportError at call time. One of T-065's six frozen tests therefore cannot pass at T-065's build time, and the obvious repair is unavailable: adding T-065 -> T-062 creates a genuine cycle, which I verified programmatically. I independently AST-swept all 120 tests - extracting each test's ticket marker, its function-level product imports, each imported module's owning ticket by scope glob, and whether that owner lies in the marked ticket's transitive dependency closure. Exactly ONE violation exists in the whole suite and this is it, so the blast radius is one test, not a class. IMPORTANT for the ruling: the frozen METRIC is unaffected either way. e6_trust_passing counts passing tests per epic, not per ticket, and this test is E6 under both markers - so once T-062 lands the test passes and the metric arrives on schedule with no amendment at all. What is actually broken is only T-065's ticket-closure bookkeeping, which is an orchestrator convention rather than a frozen artifact.
subject: test_e6_trust.py::test_verification_results_are_typed_and_route_into_the_catalog_claim_dimension

head: 40bb3617a1da8ae9caa37671cb02c5e352de34dd
proposed: RECOMMEND NO AMENDMENT. The guarantee is now covered by a live test in T-011's own suite that is stronger than the frozen static scan, and no other ticket can write migrations. Record the frozen test's limitation so no future reader mistakes its green for a complete S7 proof, and require any re-dispatch of T-011 (or any audit-loop ticket that touches db/migrations) to keep the live PUBLIC assertion. If you would rather close it in the harness, the amendment is small - drop the _EXCHANGE_ROLE_RE precondition and inspect every GRANT statement, treating a PUBLIC grantee on sealed/vault as a violation - but it costs amendment 3 plus an immediate cycle-0 re-measure for a hole nothing can currently drive through.
reason: Reported by T-011 and confirmed by the orchestrator reading the frozen bytes. The test's per-statement filter is 'if "grant" not in low or not _EXCHANGE_ROLE_RE.search(low): continue', where _EXCHANGE_ROLE_RE is r'\bexchange[a-z0-9_]*\b'. A statement such as 'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA sealed TO PUBLIC; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA sealed TO PUBLIC;' contains 'grant' but does NOT contain the token 'exchange', so it is skipped before any inspection. The schema-union regex that builds granted_schemas sits inside that same loop, so it never sees the statement either. Net effect: PUBLIC includes every role, so the exchange role inherits read access to sealed.envelopes while the frozen assertion granted_schemas == {'ledger','app'} still passes with zero violations. S7 is an explicit release blocker ('the exchange cannot read envelopes') and this is the static half of its proof. T-011 verified the bypass live against a real database before reporting it. MITIGATING FACTS, which is why I am not recommending an amendment: (1) db/migrations/** is T-011's EXCLUSIVE scope and no other ticket in the 47-ticket graph can add a migration, so the blast radius is one ticket that has already shipped; (2) T-011's own 0004 migration now revokes object-level privileges from PUBLIC, so a correct re-run repairs a breached database; (3) T-011 shipped test_no_object_in_the_four_schemas_is_granted_to_public, which asserts the property LIVE against a real cluster - strictly stronger evidence than the frozen static scan could ever provide, since it observes actual ACLs rather than parsing SQL text.
subject: test_spec_criteria.py::test_migrations_never_grant_exchange_access_to_sealed_or_vault

TO PUBLIC on sealed/vault is never inspected and granted_schemas still reads {ledger, app}. It is not being closed in the harness because: (1) db/migrations/** is T-011's exclusive scope and no other ticket in the 47-ticket graph can add a migration, bounding the exposure to one already-shipped ticket; (2) T-011's 0004 migration revokes object-level privileges from PUBLIC, so a correct re-run repairs a breached database; (3) T-011 shipped test_no_object_in_the_four_schemas_is_granted_to_public, which observes real ACLs on a live cluster — strictly stronger evidence than any static SQL text scan, since it sees actual grants rather than parsing statements. The frozen test's green is therefore evidence about the parse, not about the database, and that limitation is recorded in learnings.md so no later reader mistakes it for a complete S7 proof. Standing obligation: any re-dispatch of T-011, and any audit-loop ticket touching db/migrations, must keep the live PUBLIC assertion.

head: 1b0807705285192ffe2f7dc2623a6cb9d46d86ef

reason: T-117 is CONFIRMED real but structurally undispatchable, so it will sit open forever unless you rule. Cycle 9 already lost integration time twice to gate blindness of this class, and red-check this cycle found two ticket gates (T-111, T-123) that EXIT 0 with their defect live, which is the same failure wearing a different hat. Why a worker cannot fix it: the fix belongs at scripts/verify.sh:105, a protected path — check-branch vetoes any branch touching it, correctly and every time. The ticket's own non_goals forbid dodging that veto by relocating the logic into an unprotected file, and its fallback half (conftest.py + proxyshop_support/**) collides head-on with the in-flight bootstrap lane (T-109/T-111/T-123). reason: The approved manifest contradicts ITSELF, and I may not fix it. Replaying all seven dishonest_store.behaviours once per episode against the manifest's own published observation_weights gives 0.234 at ep2 (stated band [0.34,0.50]), 0.154 at ep4 (band [0.26,0.40]), 0.084 at ep9 (band [0.14,0.24]), 0.066 at ep12 (band [0.08,0.18]) — EVERY non-zero episode falls outside its own stated band, and the store crosses the 0.35 threshold at episode 1 rather than the intended ~4-6. head: 16d1443090f9ce01f6c67ad0c5ace487556526f0
proposed: Amend _claim_identity in .swarm-loop/acceptance/test_e4_store_agent.py to identify a provenance-bearing node by a key that exists on every such node — e.g. fall back to the node's path or type when 'key' is absent, so a Discount is identified as (type/path, value, source, ref) rather than ('None', ...). This weakens no assertion and makes nothing easier to pass: it lets the helper MATCH a node it currently cannot see, so a genuinely smuggled discount still fails. Alternative if you prefer the suite untouched: rule that discounted hosted bids are out of scope for that helper and record it, but then T-042/T-043 must be told before they build. Requires freeze --amend because the acceptance suite is hash-frozen.
reason: A FROZEN HELPER WILL FAIL ON CORRECT CODE, and it is latent only by fixture accident. T-135 (landed this cycle) tightened contracts.boundary to REQUIRE provenance on offer.discount — an unprovenanced discount is now refused, correctly, because otherwise an attacker drops the provenance block instead of relabelling it. But the frozen E4 helper _claims_in treats EVERY provenance-bearing node as a claim and _claim_identity keys it on (key, value, source, ref). A Discount has no 'key'. So the very provenance T-135 now requires makes the discount node unmatchable, and it reads as smuggled. Measured on the merged tree by the T-041 lane: frozen _claims_in on a DISCOUNTED bid -> smuggled [('None','15.0','envelope_rule','envelope:store-alpha:v3#max_discount_pct@prod-cap')]; on a COLD bid -> smuggled []. test_every_claim_in_a_hosted_bid_traces_to_a_hook_call passes TODAY only because its fixture context is cold (learned_policy=None, no intro rule) so no discount is produced. It will fail on correct code the moment a discounted hosted bid reaches that helper — which is exactly what T-042 and T-043 are scheduled to produce (learned-policy discounts). Neither the T-041 lane nor I touched the frozen suite; the lane pinned the property it does control by adding a cold-path test instead.
subject: .swarm-loop/acceptance/test_e4_store_agent.py::_claims_in / _claim_identity

head: 7279452daf19b0f04e983054382ee8df6ee5bdcf
proposed: freeze --amend tickets.json to do two things and nothing else. (a) Narrow the scope of the six tickets from the directory glob to their actual per-file ownership: T-032 -> apps/exchange/src/ranking/** + apps/exchange/tests/test_ranking.py + apps/exchange/tests/_fixtures_ranking.py; T-034 -> apps/exchange/src/policy/** + test_bandit.py + _fixtures_bandit.py; T-035 -> apps/exchange/src/reports/** + test_loss_reports.py + _fixtures_loss_reports.py; T-042 -> packages/store-agent/src/learning/** + test_learning.py + _fixtures_learning.py; T-043 -> packages/store-agent/src/modes/** + test_modes.py + _fixtures_modes.py; T-044 -> packages/store-agent/src/external/** + test_external_bids.py + _fixtures_external.py. This WEAKENS NOTHING: it makes check-wave's veto sharper, not looser - two lanes that would genuinely write the same file are still refused, and no lane gains the right to touch a file it could not touch before. (b) Drop the three paper edges T-034->T-032, T-035->T-032, T-045->T-044, each of which I verified against the frozen test body rather than the ticket prose. If you would rather not touch depends_on, (a) alone is worth having: it takes the store-agent trio from three waves to one. If you decline both, say so and I will serialize them - it costs cycles, not correctness.
reason: THE GRAPH IS SERIALIZING SIX INDEPENDENT BUILDS, AND THAT IS WHY THE TWO LARGEST METRICS HAVE NEVER MOVED. Measured this cycle, all of it against HEAD 7279452. (1) The 44 red acceptance tests are dominated by E4 (5/20) and E3 (9/21), 27 of the 44. Independent diagnosis of both epics found that EVERY one of those 27 failures is an ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError — not one assertion is reached — because seven whole packages were never written: apps/exchange/src/{ranking,policy,reports}/ and packages/store-agent/src/{learning,modes,external}/ are 0-byte __init__.py files with no siblings, and apps/seller-reference/src/ holds only __init__.py. The tickets that own them (T-032, T-034, T-035, T-042, T-043, T-044, T-045) are all open with every dependency closed, and dispatch.jsonl has ZERO records naming T-042, T-043, T-044 or T-045 across all 114 entries. They were never dispatched in thirteen cycles. (2) The reason is mechanical, not a judgement call. Each of T-032/T-034/T-035 declares scope 'apps/exchange/tests/**' and each of T-042/T-043/T-044 declares 'packages/store-agent/tests/**', so check-wave correctly vetoes every pair of them on a glob intersection - T-032<->T-034, T-032<->T-035, T-034<->T-035, T-042<->T-043, T-042<->T-044, T-043<->T-044. Their REAL ownership is disjoint: test_ranking.py / test_bandit.py / test_loss_reports.py, and test_external_bids.py / test_learning.py / test_modes.py, and each tests directory's conftest.py auto-loads uniquely-named _fixtures_<topic>.py siblings so no lane need edit a shared file. The glob is coarser than the truth, and the veto that follows from it is what keeps only one of each trio in flight. (3) Three depends_on edges are contradicted by the frozen tests themselves: T-034->T-032 and T-035->T-032 (both read in full; the policy and reports tests import nothing from ranking and feed plain fixture dicts) and T-045->T-044 (the persona test imports only the personas module and the manifest - no signing, no door, no queue). I have dispatched the largest legal wave the current globs permit - T-032, T-044, T-045, check-wave OK - so the run is moving regardless of how you rule. What is blocked is the OTHER four, which under the current graph need three more serialized waves to do work that has no real ordering between it.
subject: tickets.json — scope globs and depends_on edges on T-032/T-034/T-035 and T-042/T-043/T-044/T-045
